Bike Build · Building a Dream

The charity bike build activity that brings the whole room to its feet.

Building a Dream is our flagship charity bike build team building event, where your team races the clock to build real, road-ready bikes from the frame up, then the children who receive them ride into the room. It’s the moment your people remember for years. It’s one of our signature charity & CSR team building events.

What it is

Building a Dream, in a nutshell.

Building a Dream is a hands-on challenge with a heart. As bike team building goes, this bicycle team building activity puts a real give-back at its center: teams earn parts, solve problems and assemble complete, road-ready bikes — and just when they think the activity is over, the kids arrive to receive them.

Collaboration under pressure

Teams self-organize, divide work and problem-solve against the clock.

A shared peak moment

The reveal is the emotional high everyone retells back at the office.

Purpose people feel

Your team built something real for a child — pride that carries back to work.

Works at any size

From 5 to 5,000, scaled to your room.

At a glance

The details planners ask for.

  • Duration~2 hours typical · 60 min to 4 hours · can anchor a multi-day theme
  • Group size5 to 5,000 — no maximum
  • FormatIndoor; theater seating with build tables
  • Skill neededNone — every bike is safety-checked by our crew
  • What your team buildsComplete, road-ready bikes
  • What each child receivesA bike, helmet, lock, and backpack
  • Setup & teardownFully managed by our event crew
  • AvailabilityOnsite, nationwide, since 2003
How it works

Three moves from bag-of-parts to unforgettable.

1

Frame the day, then team up

Your people start in theater seating for a short, customizable opener that connects the build to your message, then split into teams of five and compete in quick challenges to earn their bike’s components.

2

Build a real bike

Teams move to the tables and assemble a complete, road-ready bike from the frame up, following a clear kit. Our crew safety-checks every finished bike. No experience needed.

3

The reveal & the human tunnel

The children who will receive the bikes arrive. Your team forms a human tunnel, and the kids ride in through it on the bikes your people just built. The room goes from focused to unforgettable in seconds — then everyone returns to their seats for the wrap-up.

What your team takes back

It looks like a bike build. It debriefs like leadership training.

The build is the story; the wrap-up is where it turns into behavior. Facilitators tie the experience to the themes your team is working on — here are four we return to most.

Service

Every team called their bike race-ready. Then they saw the child’s face, picked their tools back up, and found the extra 3–5% that makes all the difference.

Continual improvement

One turn of the wrench isn’t sexy. Ten turns is a safe bike. Small, repeated effort is what actually ships — on a bike and at work.

Leadership

A leader’s smallest “turn of the wrench” lands on the people around them — sometimes small, sometimes large, always an impact. Are we choosing those actions carefully?

Dreams

When did “be practical” replace “what do you dream about?” What are your dreams now — and whose are you helping come true?
The reason it sticks

Your team builds something real — for a child who needs it.

Every bike is donated to a child in your community, often onsite. For a child who would never own one, a bike is freedom, independence and responsibility. Each one comes with a helmet, lock and backpack — and your team doesn’t just bond, they change a kid’s day in the same afternoon.

And the impact may outlast the day: a 2015 study found that low-income urban students who walked or biked more than half a mile to school had 65% lower odds of being overweight or obese than students who did not actively commute.DeWeese, R. S., & Ohri-Vachaspati, P. (2015). “The Role of Distance in Examining the Association Between Active Commuting to School and Students’ Weight Status.” Journal of Physical Activity and Health, 12(9), 1280–1288. doi:10.1123/jpah.2014-0100. Observational, cross-sectional study — shows association, not causation.

Questions, answered

Building a Dream FAQs

What is a bike build team building activity? +

A bike build is a hands-on team building activity where groups assemble real, road-ready bikes that are then donated to children in need. Our version, Building a Dream, ends with the children arriving onsite to receive the bikes.

How many people can do Building a Dream? +

From 5 to 5,000, including conference general sessions. There is no maximum — it is our most-requested large-group activity and scales cleanly.

Do participants need any technical skill? +

None. Every bike comes with a clear kit and our team safety-checks each finished bike. Anyone can take part.

How long does it take? +

About two hours is typical. We run Building a Dream anywhere from 60 minutes to four hours, and it can anchor a multi-day conference theme. We tailor the length to your agenda — a fast 60-minute build is pure hands-on assembly, while a longer session adds framing and debrief.

What does each child receive? +

Each child receives a complete, road-ready bike your team built, plus a helmet, lock and backpack — and, at most events, they come onsite to receive it in person.

Can Building a Dream be a conference theme? +

Yes. It scales to a conference general session for up to 5,000 people and can anchor a multi-day event theme, with the opener and debrief tied to your meeting’s message.

Is this a charity bike build? +

Yes. Building a Dream is a charity bike build. Every bike your team assembles is donated to a child in need, so it doubles as a build a bike for charity event and a high-energy team building challenge.

How does a charity bike build team building event work? +

A bike build team building event runs in three moves. Teams earn parts in quick challenges, follow a clear kit for the team building bike assembly, then meet the children who ride away on the finished bikes. No technical skill is needed.

What’s included? +

Everything to run it end to end: a lead facilitator and event crew, all build materials and kits, the charitable donation of what your team builds, plus full setup and teardown. You bring the room and your people; we bring the rest.

How much does it cost? +

Pricing depends on your group size and city, and it’s set per participant with the charitable donation included. Tell us your group and we’ll send a tailored proposal, usually within a business day.
